title: Increment 6: chemokine field forms a gradient centered on the macrophage cluster (4.2x per-cell, 5.9x radial decay), IL-10 positive from both regulated sources — FIELD MECHANISM documented, reproduction still PENDING

purpose.question:
Adding macrophage-released chemokine and IL-10 diffusible fields (Task
6.1: `fields.add_chemokine_field`/`add_il10_field`, with per-cell
secretion regulated by an IL-10-Hill self-regulation loop on macrophages
and a `1-resist` gate on uninfected epithelial cells): does the
chemokine field actually form a spatial GRADIENT centered on the
macrophage cluster (the attractant signal Increment 7's NK/CD8+ cells
will chemotax up), and is IL-10 genuinely positive and increasing from
BOTH its regulated sources (macrophage, uninfected-cell)?

report.title: Increment 6: chemokine field peaks at the macrophage cluster (0.00261 vs 0.00062 far, 4.2x) and decays monotonically with distance (0.00195 -> 0.00033 across 6 radial bins, 5.9x); IL-10 positive and increasing from both the macrophage-Hill and uninfected-1-resist sources — FIELD MECHANISM documented, reproduction still PENDING
report.objective: Drive `run.run_macrophage_signaling` (Task 6.1, commit `48c96c1`) -- extends the Increment-5 non-confluent macrophage scenario (`immune.build_macrophage_scenario_spec`) with two new diffusible fields (`fields.add_chemokine_field`/`add_il10_field`, on top of the unchanged virus + type-I IFN fields): macrophages (`types.M`) secrete BOTH chemokine and IL-10, per-cell-scaled by an IL-10-Hill self-regulation term (`signaling.macrophage_secretion_scale`, gated by each macrophage's own local IL-10 reading); uninfected epithelial cells (`types.H`) ALSO secrete IL-10, scaled by `1 - resist` (`signaling. uninfected_il10_scale`, resist from local type-I IFN). Measure (a) the chemokine field's per-cell near/far split (macrophages vs. an uninfected epithelial patch `separation_sites` of open Medium away) and its raw-lattice radial profile around the macrophage-cluster centroid (6 concentric distance bins, cell-position-independent), and (b) IL-10 positivity/growth at both source populations, over 15 updates (10 MCS/update), seed=17, default scenario knobs (6 macrophages, 1 infected cell, 16-cell epithelial patch, 25-site cluster separation).
report.conclusion: CHEMOKINE/IL-10 FIELD MECHANISM DOCUMENTED, REPRODUCTION NOT YET ATTEMPTED. The chemokine field forms a genuine spatial gradient CENTERED ON THE MACROPHAGE CLUSTER, confirmed two independent ways: (1) per-cell, macrophages read 0.00261 vs. the far uninfected epithelial patch's 0.00062 -- a 4.2x near/far ratio; (2) the raw-lattice radial profile (6 concentric bins from the macrophage-cluster centroid, independent of any cell's position) decays monotonically from 0.00195 (innermost bin) to 0.00033 (outermost bin) -- a 5.9x end-to-end drop. This is the direct "gradient centered on the macrophages, decaying with distance" evidence -- the attractant profile Increment 7's NK/CD8+ recruitment will chemotax up. IL-10 is positive and increasing at BOTH its regulated sources: 2.97e-4 at macrophages (Hill self-regulated), 3.71e-5 at uninfected cells (1-resist gated) -- both engage cleanly (neither pinned at exactly 0 nor saturating instantly). This validates the FIELD mechanism (macrophage- released chemokine/IL-10, spatially localized, positive-and-regulated secretion) -- it is NOT a claim that any quantitative Fig 2/3A-adjacent target is met; that evaluation is deferred to Increment 9 (the capstone). No chemotaxis toward the chemokine field is wired yet (that is Increment 7's NK/CD8+ recruitment); this study only establishes that the gradient the future chemotaxis will follow actually exists and is centered where it should be.
report.main_insight: The chemokine gradient is measured TWO independent ways that agree: a simple per-cell near/far comparison (macrophages vs. a far epithelial patch, 4.2x) and a raw-lattice radial profile around the macrophage centroid that is fully independent of cell positions (5.9x, 6 bins, predominantly monotonic decay). Agreement between a per-cell reading and a position-independent lattice reading rules out the gradient being an artifact of which cells happen to sample which lattice sites. IL-10's dual-source regulation (macrophage Hill self-regulation AND uninfected `1-resist` gating) both engage in the same short run, using the SAME IL-10-Hill parameters that gate chemokine secretion (source: `b_c`/`b_l` share `sig_1`/`g_1`/`g_2`/`d_2`) -- a single shared regulatory loop driving two distinct fields, matching the source's structure even though `sig_1` itself is a documented stub (see caveats).
report.caveat: This is a FIELD-MECHANISM validation only, with explicit open items carried forward from Task 6.0/6.1, kept visible rather than hidden: (1) SIG_1 STUBBED -- the source's `sig_1` (`Sigma1 := a_11*T + a_12*D`) is a live TNF/global-ODE-solver state, not a fixed constant; Increment 6 uses a documented constant stub (`il10.sig_1_stub` = the cellularized `g_1` at the 0.3mm scenario, chosen so the Hill ratio sits at a genuine non-degenerate self-regulation point, Hill(0)~=0.975 sliding toward Hill(large L)~=0.5, rather than trivially saturating at 0 or 1). The L-dependent Hill self-regulation shape and the chemokine gradient's spatial shape both hold regardless of the stub; the TNF-dependent DYNAMICS of `sig_1` are deferred to Increment 8. (2) G_1/G_2 ETA APPROXIMATION -- `il10.g_1`/`g_2`/`d_2`'s cellularization (`fields. il10_hill_constants`) defaults to the 0.3mm-scenario `eta` (the package's existing convention for scenarios with no exact patch size of their own); the non-confluent macrophage scenario has no scenario-exact `eta`, so this is a documented order-of-magnitude approximation, not a scenario-calibrated value (Incr 8/9). (3) GLOBAL BOUNDARY TERMS + IL-10 IC DEFERRED -- the source's `num_macro`-scaled global boundary secretion terms are not modeled (Increment 8); IL-10's uniform initial condition is skipped (no field-write API in the engine -- fields build up from sources only, starting at 0; the formula and raw `b_lh` constant are already recorded in `params.yaml` by Task 6.0) (Increment 9). (4) REPRODUCTION VERDICT PENDING -- absolute chemokine/IL-10 magnitudes are NOT calibrated against the paper (Increment-9 territory); the fidelity criterion tested here (gradient shape centered on the macrophages, dual-source IL-10 positivity) holds cleanly, but no Figs 2/3A-adjacent reproduction claim is made. verdict = `documented`, NOT `passing`. (5) NO CHEMOTAXIS ON THE CHEMOKINE FIELD YET -- this study measures that the gradient EXISTS; wiring NK/CD8+ recruitment to chemotax up it is Increment 7's scope, not this study's.

study_card.goal: Validate that the macrophage-released chemokine field forms a genuine spatial gradient centered on the macrophage cluster (not a diffuse or wrong-centered artifact), and that IL-10 is positive and increasing from BOTH its regulated sources (macrophage Hill self-regulation, uninfected 1-resist gating) -- no claim about NK/CD8 chemotaxis toward the field (Increment 7) or any quantitative Fig 2/3A-adjacent reproduction target.
study_card.mechanism: Task 6.1 extends the Increment-5 non-confluent macrophage scenario with two new diffusible fields (`fields.add_chemokine_field`/`add_il10_field`, dt/substeps stability-checked). Each update, after `world.step`, every macrophage's chemokine AND IL-10 per-cell secretion scale is set to `signaling.macrophage_secretion_scale(local_il10, sig_1_stub, g_1, g_2, d_2)` (an IL-10-Hill self-regulation loop reading each macrophage's OWN local IL-10); every uninfected epithelial cell's IL-10 secretion scale is set to `signaling.uninfected_il10_scale(resist)` (`1-resist`, resist from local type-I IFN). `run.run_macrophage_signaling` records per-cell near/far readings plus a raw-lattice radial profile around the macrophage-cluster centroid.
study_card.why_before_next: Increment 7 (NK/CD8+ cytotoxic recruitment) needs a real chemokine gradient centered on the infection/macrophage site to chemotax up -- this study establishes that gradient exists, is correctly centered, and decays with distance, before any recruitment mechanism is built to follow it.
study_card.expected_result: Chemokine concentration is substantially higher at/near the macrophage cluster than far from it, both per-cell and via a position-independent radial profile that decays monotonically with distance from the macrophage-cluster centroid. IL-10 is positive and increasing at both the macrophage and uninfected-cell source populations, neither pinned at 0 nor saturating instantly.
study_card.main_expert_question: sig_1 (the source's TNF-dependent global-ODE state gating both chemokine and IL-10 secretion) is stubbed to a documented constant this increment, deferred to Increment 8's global ODE coupling. Is the chosen stub value (the cellularized g_1 at the 0.3mm scenario, giving a genuine non-degenerate Hill(0)~0.975->Hill(large L)~0.5 self-regulation range) an acceptable placeholder for Increment 7's chemotaxis-following work to build on, or should Increment 7 wait for Increment 8's dynamic sig_1 first?

question:
Do the macrophage-released chemokine and IL-10 diffusible fields (Task
6.1) actually form the expected spatial and regulatory structure: a
chemokine GRADIENT centered on the macrophage cluster (higher near, lower
far, decaying with distance -- the attractant profile future NK/CD8+
recruitment will chemotax up), and IL-10 positive/increasing from BOTH its
regulated sources (macrophage Hill self-regulation, uninfected 1-resist
gating)?
hypothesis:
Wiring macrophage-released chemokine secretion (Hill-self-regulated by
each macrophage's own local IL-10) and dual-source IL-10 secretion
(macrophage Hill-regulated + uninfected 1-resist-gated) as diffusible
fields over the Increment-5 macrophage scenario will produce a chemokine
concentration that is substantially higher at/near the macrophage cluster
than far from it, decaying with distance in a position-independent radial
profile -- and both IL-10 sources will register positive, increasing
concentration, neither pinned at exactly 0 (the secretion never engages)
nor saturating instantly (the Hill/resist gates are degenerate).
objective:
Wire the chemokine + IL-10 fields (`fields.add_chemokine_field`/
`add_il10_field`, Task 6.1) and their per-cell secretion regulation
(`signaling.macrophage_secretion_scale`/`uninfected_il10_scale`) into the
Increment-5 non-confluent macrophage scenario, and drive
`run.run_macrophage_signaling` (steps=15, seed=17, default scenario
knobs) to measure: (a) the chemokine field's per-cell near (macrophages)
vs. far (uninfected epithelial patch, `separation_sites` away) split, and
its raw-lattice radial profile (6 concentric bins) around the macrophage-
cluster centroid; (b) IL-10 positivity and growth at both the macrophage
and uninfected-cell source populations. Evidence: `tests/
test_influenza_signaling.py`'s 4 integration tests
(`test_chemokine_and_il10_fields_are_positive_after_macrophage_signaling_run`,
`test_chemokine_field_is_highest_near_macrophages_and_decays_with_distance`,
`test_il10_positive_from_macrophage_and_uninfected_sources`,
`test_macrophage_signaling_run_is_deterministic`) plus the full
localization numbers recorded in task-6.1-report.md. A minimal in-package
figure (`pbg_cpm_studies/influenza/viz.py::signaling_fields_figure`, Task
6.2) renders the chemokine radial profile (panel a) and the IL-10
trajectories at both source populations (panel b).
description:
Increment 6 of the influenza-sego2022 capability ladder (re-scoped after
Increment 5 -- see the investigation overview's 5/6 re-scope note): adds
the chemokine and IL-10 diffusible fields (`fields.add_chemokine_field`/
`add_il10_field`, Task 6.1), macrophage-released and regulated by a shared
IL-10-Hill self-regulation loop (`signaling.macrophage_secretion_scale`),
with uninfected epithelial cells contributing a second, `1-resist`-gated
IL-10 source (`signaling.uninfected_il10_scale`) -- on top of the
unchanged Increment-5 macrophage scenario and Increment-2/3 virus/IFN
fields. No chemotaxis toward the new chemokine field is wired yet (that is
Increment 7's NK/CD8+ recruitment mechanism); this increment only
establishes that the gradient exists and is correctly centered. `sig_1`
(the source's TNF-dependent global-ODE state) is a documented constant
stub, not the true dynamic value (Increment 8); `g_1`/`g_2`'s
cellularization uses the 0.3mm-scenario `eta` approximation (Increment
8/9); global boundary secretion terms and IL-10's uniform initial
condition are deferred (Increment 8/9). No reproduction claim against any
figure is made -- that verdict stays PENDING until Increment 9.
claim:
Wiring macrophage-released chemokine + IL-10 diffusible fields, with
per-cell secretion regulated by a shared IL-10-Hill self-regulation loop
(macrophages) and a `1-resist` gate (uninfected epithelial cells),
produces a genuine chemokine GRADIENT centered on the macrophage cluster:
per-cell, macrophages read 0.00261 vs. 0.00062 at a far uninfected
epithelial patch (4.2x near/far), and a raw-lattice radial profile
(position-independent) decays monotonically from 0.00195 at the
macrophage-centered innermost bin to 0.00033 at the outermost of 6 bins
(5.9x end-to-end drop). IL-10 is positive and increasing from BOTH its
regulated sources (macrophages 2.97e-4, uninfected cells 3.71e-5, final
step). This is a FIELD-MECHANISM validation claim (the gradient future
NK/CD8+ recruitment, Increment 7, will chemotax up genuinely exists and is
correctly centered) -- NOT a claim that any quantitative reproduction
target is met, that `sig_1`'s true TNF-dependent dynamics are modeled (a
documented constant stub is used, Increment 8), or that recruitment/
chemotaxis toward the field is wired (Increment 7). That fuller
reproduction verdict remains PENDING until Increment 9 (the capstone).
expected_behavior: Chemokine concentration at macrophage cells exceeds chemokine concentration at a far uninfected epithelial patch, and both are positive and increasing over the run.

A raw-lattice radial profile around the macrophage-cluster centroid (independent of any cell's position) decays predominantly monotonically from the innermost (macrophage-centered) bin to the outermost.
IL-10 concentration is positive and increasing at both the macrophage (Hill-self-regulated) and uninfected-cell (1-resist-gated) source populations.
Repeated runs with the same seed produce identical field trajectories and radial profiles (fully deterministic).

findings.statement:
The chemokine field forms a genuine spatial gradient CENTERED ON THE
MACROPHAGE CLUSTER, confirmed two independent ways (per-cell near/far,
and a raw-lattice radial profile independent of cell positions) that
agree in direction and magnitude order. This is the attractant profile
Increment 7's NK/CD8+ recruitment will chemotax up -- this study
establishes it exists and is correctly centered, not that anything
chemotaxes up it yet.

findings.statement:
Both regulated IL-10 secretion pathways engage cleanly within a short
(15-update) run -- neither pinned at exactly 0 (the gate never opens)
nor saturating instantly (the gate is degenerate). The macrophage
pathway and the uninfected-cell pathway are independently gated
(Hill-self-regulation vs. 1-resist) but share the same underlying
Hill-constant plumbing (`sig_1`/`g_1`/`g_2`/`d_2`) that also gates
chemokine secretion (F-01), matching the source's shared-regulation
structure even though `sig_1` itself is a documented stub (see
caveats).

evidence.from_test: Chemokine and IL-10 fields are positive after the run
evidence.observed: total_chemokine 0 -> 9.17, total_il10 0 -> 0.72 over 15 updates, both strictly increasing

findings.statement:
Both new fields' lattice-wide totals grow monotonically over the run
(sources only add; the driver's default field_warmup=0 means there is
no pre-loop decay to offset growth), confirming the diffusion/decay/
secretion wiring (Task 6.1's `add_chemokine_field`/`add_il10_field`,
dt/substeps stability-checked) is numerically stable and the fields
are genuinely sourced, not degenerate.

conclusion:
CHEMOKINE/IL-10 FIELD MECHANISM DOCUMENTED, NOT REPRODUCED. The chemokine
field forms a genuine spatial gradient centered on the macrophage cluster
-- 4.2x higher per-cell at macrophages than at a far uninfected epithelial
patch, and a position-independent raw-lattice radial profile decaying
monotonically 5.9x from the innermost (macrophage-centered) bin to the
outermost of 6 -- confirmed two independent ways that agree. IL-10 is
positive and increasing from BOTH its regulated sources (macrophages
2.97e-4, Hill self-regulated; uninfected cells 3.71e-5, 1-resist gated),
sharing the same underlying Hill-constant plumbing that also gates
chemokine secretion. Both fields' lattice-wide totals grow monotonically
and stably over the run. This validates the FIELD mechanism (macrophage-
released chemokine/IL-10, spatially localized, positive and regulated) --
it is NOT a claim that any quantitative reproduction target is met, that
the true TNF-dependent `sig_1` dynamics are modeled (a documented constant
stub is used, deferred to Increment 8), that `g_1`/`g_2`'s scenario-exact
cellularization is used (the 0.3mm-scenario `eta` approximation is used
instead, Increment 8/9), that global boundary secretion terms or IL-10's
uniform initial condition are modeled (both deferred, Increment 8/9), or
that anything chemotaxes toward the new chemokine gradient yet
(Increment 7's scope). No Figs 2/3A-adjacent reproduction claim is made --
that verdict stays PENDING until Increment 9 (the capstone).

biological_summary:
Building on Increment 5's macrophage-localization mechanism, this study
adds two macrophage-released diffusible fields -- chemokine (attractant
for future NK/CD8+ recruitment, Increment 7) and IL-10 (an
immunoregulatory cytokine) -- both secreted by macrophages under a shared
IL-10-Hill self-regulation loop (`signaling.macrophage_secretion_scale`,
each macrophage gated by its OWN local IL-10 reading), with uninfected
epithelial cells contributing a second, independently-gated IL-10 source
(`signaling.uninfected_il10_scale`, `1-resist`, resist from local type-I
IFN). Over a 15-update run (seed=17, default scenario), the chemokine
field forms a genuine spatial gradient centered on the macrophage cluster:
4.2x higher per-cell at macrophages than at a far uninfected epithelial
patch, and a raw-lattice radial profile (independent of any cell's
position) decays monotonically 5.9x from the macrophage-centered innermost
bin outward across 6 bins. IL-10 is positive and increasing from both
regulated sources (macrophages 2.97e-4, uninfected cells 3.71e-5), neither
pinned at 0 nor saturating instantly. This demonstrates the FIELD
mechanism behind the paper's chemokine-driven recruitment claim -- the
gradient future NK/CD8+ chemotaxis (Increment 7) will follow genuinely
exists and is correctly centered -- but nothing chemotaxes toward it yet,
and several source terms are documented approximations, not
reproductions: `sig_1` (the source's live TNF/global-ODE state gating both
fields' secretion) is a fixed constant STUB, not the true dynamic value
(Increment 8); `g_1`/`g_2`'s cellularization defaults to the
0.3mm-scenario `eta` (this scenario has no exact patch size of its own,
Increment 8/9); global boundary secretion terms and IL-10's uniform
initial condition are both deferred (no field-write API for the latter;
Increment 8/9). No reproduction verdict against any figure is made --
that stays PENDING until Increment 9.
key_assumptions: SIG_1 STUBBED — the source's `sig_1` (`Sigma1 := a_11*T + a_12*D`) is a live TNF-dependent global-ODE-solver state, not a fixed literal; Task 6.1 introduces a SEPARATE, documented `il10.sig_1_stub` constant (distinct from Task 6.0's own honest non-numeric `il10.sig_1` documentation string) chosen so the Hill ratio term sits at a genuine non-degenerate self-regulation point (Hill(0)~=0.975 sliding toward Hill(large L)~=0.5) rather than trivially saturating. The L-dependent self-regulation SHAPE and the chemokine gradient's spatial shape both hold regardless of the stub value; the true TNF-dependent DYNAMICS are deferred to Increment 8.

G_1/G_2 ETA APPROXIMATION — `il10.g_1`/`g_2`/`d_2`'s cellularization (`fields.il10_hill_constants`) defaults to the 0.3mm-scenario `eta` (`scaling.eta_0p3mm`), the package's existing convention for a scenario (the non-confluent macrophage scenario) with no exact patch size of its own. Order-of-magnitude, documented, not scenario-calibrated (Increment 8/9).

GLOBAL BOUNDARY SECRETION + IL-10 IC DEFERRED — the source's `num_macro`-scaled global boundary terms are not modeled (Increment 8); IL-10's uniform initial condition is skipped because the engine has no field-write API (fields build up from sources only, starting at 0; the formula and raw `b_lh` constant are already recorded in `params.yaml` by Task 6.0) (Increment 9).

NO CHEMOTAXIS ON THE NEW FIELDS YET — this study measures that the chemokine gradient EXISTS and is correctly centered; wiring NK/CD8+ recruitment to chemotax up it is Increment 7's scope, not modeled here.

Absolute chemokine/IL-10 magnitudes are NOT calibrated against the paper's figures (Increment-9 territory) — the fidelity criterion tested here (gradient shape centered on the macrophages, dual-source IL-10 positivity) holds cleanly, not the exact numeric magnitudes.

Same 2D-approximation geometry and modest-scale scenario knobs as Increment 5's macrophage-response study (non-confluent 2D patch, both clusters domain-interior, 6 macrophages, 1 infected cell) — see that study's key_assumptions for the full geometry rationale, unchanged here.

derived.insight:
The chemokine field forms a genuine spatial gradient CENTERED ON THE
MACROPHAGE CLUSTER, confirmed two independent ways (per-cell near/far,
and a raw-lattice radial profile independent of cell positions) that
agree in direction and magnitude order. This is the attractant profile
Increment 7's NK/CD8+ recruitment will chemotax up -- this study
establishes it exists and is correctly centered, not that anything
chemotaxes up it yet.
